mpi.name: NBS Nigeria Multidimensional Poverty Index
mpi.note: Tables D6 and D7, printed pages 100–104. Fieldwork 2021–2022. Survey estimates, not a current census. Borno results are not representative. Confidence intervals retained. The source repeats Osun West identically in D7; retained once after all 11 values matched.

codes.name: NBS MPI survey district codebook
codes.note: Official NBS survey identifiers (a1b), not INEC delimitation codes. District-to-state association checked against state names and NBS state-code prefix.

lga.name: GRID3 operational LGA boundaries
lga.note: 774 operational LGA polygons. March 2021 release; not certified electoral boundaries. Geometry simplified to 0.002 degrees for this display and raster aggregation.

states.name: geoBoundaries / GRID3 state boundaries
states.note: Pinned existing local NGA-ADM1-27671186, commit 9469f09. 37 explicit state-name mappings. Map does not show electoral boundaries.

population.name: WorldPop 2020 UN-adjusted population
population.note: Approximate 1 km raster population summed by GRID3 LGA using pixel-centre assignment. Rounded estimates; boundary mismatch leaves some raster population unassigned. State estimates sum assigned LGAs. Not census counts or 2026 forecasts.

health.name: GRID3 health facilities v4.0
health.note: Counts of listed facilities, not verified functioning facilities. October 2026 release. Non-exhaustive and not fully government-validated. State/LGA name matching only; unmatched records disclosed.

projects.name: BudgIT / Tracka 2023 FG projects analysis
projects.note: Printed page 10: state-attributed ZIP allocations and project counts. Rounded allocated budgets, not releases, payments or completed projects. Some projects are not attributable to a state. Project example on printed page 2 is illustrative coverage only.
projects.license: Published budget facts extracted with attribution; report remains with publisher

programme.name: Nigeria G2P sandbox aggregate snapshot
programme.note: Allowlisted aggregate counts from this demonstration installation only. Not Nigerian national programme coverage, eligibility, payment or settlement evidence. No personal records published.

simulation.name: User-controlled planning scenario
simulation.note: Illustrative budget × assumed multiplier. Neither an economic forecast nor a causal impact estimate. Never added to published figures.

state_economy.license: World Bank published statistical facts, attributed to NBS and World Bank; original report retained by publisher.
state_economy.name: World Bank / NBS state economy, Box 1
state_economy.note: October 2025 Nigeria Development Update, printed page 5. Rounded 2023 figures explicitly printed in the text only: GDP totals for 3 states, national GDP shares for 6, and GDP per capita for 6. Incomplete coverage; not a national ranking. GDP per capita is output per person, not household income or salary. Published per-capita figures are retained; the atlas does not divide 2023 GDP by its 2020 population layer.

state_sectors.license: World Bank published statistical facts, attributed to NBS and World Bank; original report retained by publisher.
state_sectors.name: World Bank / NBS sector shares, Annex 3
state_sectors.note: October 2025 Nigeria Development Update, printed page 53. The three reported leading sectors for all 36 states and FCT, as shares of each state’s 2023 GDP. Not a complete sector breakdown. An unlisted sector is unknown, not zero. Crop and livestock are separate agricultural activities, not total agriculture. Source labels and values retained; charts sort by numeric share (the source lists Sokoto’s second and third sectors out of size order). No LGA or constituency allocation.

nbs_2017.name: NBS State Nominal GDP, May 2019 appendix
nbs_2017.note: Historical 2017 current-basic-price accounts for 22 states/FCT only. PDF page 186 (2017 appendix). Original table amounts are NGN million, converted to NGN. This is not the rebased 2023 series. Appendix Akwa Ibom GDP (5,142,862.45 million) differs from page 3 summary (5,141,068.15 million); appendix value retained and reconciliation disclosed. Printed dashes stay unavailable, not zero. Parent sectors and child activities are never added together. No matched population denominator or per-capita estimate supplied.
nbs_2017.license: Published statistical facts extracted with attribution; original document remains with publisher.

jigawa_2023.name: Jigawa State Bureau of Statistics: GDP 2019–2023
jigawa_2023.note: PDF page 2 supplies GDP at current basic prices in NGN million. Detailed sector series on PDF pages 7–18 are used; page 6 supplies broad aggregates. The page 3 infographic says agriculture 33.60%, conflicting with 36.60% on pages 6 and 7; the repeated detailed-series figure is retained with this qualification. State report differs from the World Bank Annex 3 series and is kept separate. No matched 2023 population denominator or GDP-per-person figure verified.
jigawa_2023.license: Published statistical facts extracted with attribution; original document remains with publisher.

delta_2022.name: Delta State GDP 2021 & 2022 report
delta_2022.note: Tables 3.1a (printed pages 8–9) and 3.3 (page 25). Sector values and GDP at current basic prices; a separate GDP at market prices includes net indirect product taxes. GDP per person uses the report’s 2022 market-price GDP and projected population. The report calls it per-capita income, but it is GDP divided by population, not measured household income. Different vintage and year from the World Bank 2023 series; never combined for rankings. Blank activity rows remain unavailable.
delta_2022.license: Published statistical facts extracted with attribution; original document remains with publisher.

gaps: Governor directory covers all 36 states; FCT minister is appointed. State assembly evidence covers 36 states, including partial rosters, dated reports and unresolved source labels. Remaining assembly members and local council heads are not verified. Boundaries and tenure dates remain incomplete.
No validated LGA/ward-to-constituency crosswalk or constituency polygons loaded. State association is not a spatial allocation rule.
No constituency GDP, GVA, income, employment, or live treasury feed is asserted.
Population, poverty, facilities and budgets refer to different years; they are not a synchronized current snapshot.

Economic evidence is state-level and partial: 3 GDP totals, 6 national shares, 6 GDP-per-capita figures and top-three sector shares for 37 areas (2023). Household per-capita income and complete sector accounts are unavailable. No economic values are allocated to LGAs or constituencies.

Separate economic-report library: NBS 2017 accounts for 22 states/FCT, Jigawa 2023 and Delta 2022. These vintages are not merged into the World Bank 2023 comparisons. NGF 2023 profiles add published GDP for all 36 states, with unspecified price basis; FCT retains its separate historical report. Complete matched-year GDP and per-capita coverage remains unavailable.

gdp.qualification: Lagos Economic Development Update 2025: printed page 29 (PDF page 30) projects 2024 real GDP per person at US$5,043; Figure 2.12 labels the measure PPP. Printed page 59 (PDF page 60) projects 2024 nominal GDP at NGN54.77 trillion. Both are forecasts, not observed outcomes. Nominal GDP and real PPP GDP per person use different price bases; do not divide one by the other to infer population. Real/PPP base year is not stated in these passages.

Printed page 59 (PDF page 60) projects 2024 nominal GDP at NGN54.77 trillion. Both are forecasts, not observed outcomes. Nominal GDP and real PPP GDP per person use different price bases; do not divide one by the other to infer population. Real/PPP base year is not stated in these passages.

notes: Publisher forecast for 2024, issued in its 2025 report; not a confirmed actual GDP or income observation.
GDP is nominal naira; GDP per person is real purchasing-power-parity US dollars. These measures must not be used together to infer population.
The real/PPP base year and a full quantitative sector breakdown are not verified here. Kept outside all comparable-series rankings.

methodology: Names and seats are publisher-listed officeholders, checked on 2026-11-04; directory rows have no effective dates. This is a dated snapshot, not a live certified electoral register.
Senate, federal constituencies and state assembly seats are separate geographies. Only exact normalized state-and-district matches link to the existing atlas.

Bill counts are atlas aggregates of the NALTF public bill feed. Attribution requires the same chamber and exact normalized name tokens (order ignored); no fuzzy name matching or transfer from previous occupants.

Only bills with first-reading dates from 13 June 2023 to 2026-11-04 are included. Duplicate chamber/bill-number records and bill-prefix/chamber conflicts are excluded. Missing dates, unmatched names and former members are excluded.
Stages reflect the publisher’s latest status at the snapshot, not necessarily events during the selected first-reading year. Passed does not mean presidential assent or implementation.

A bill count measures documented activity, not legislative quality, impact, attendance or personal project delivery. No composite score, league table or causal attribution of GDP/poverty is calculated.

No matched evidence is unavailable, not zero. Zero stage counts mean zero among the linked records only. Attendance needs sittings attended / eligible sittings; oversight needs committee evidence; project delivery needs verified project and implementing-agency records.

Activity records are dated official self-reports or attributed news reports with reviewed named-person attribution, not independent outcome audits. Publisher and qualifications appear on each record. Counts are documented records, not complete totals or attendance rates. Approvals and planned inspections do not establish completed projects.
